Maintenance Report — MNT-0123-009

Asset: WELL-0123 (NE-07 Well 123, T200, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: downhole pump Work started: 06 Mar 2026 08:00 · Finished: 16 Mar 2026 21:00 · Well stopped for this job: 253 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Brian Coleman · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0123-0064 on 2026-03-05 Report written: 17 Mar 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that the wellhead was cold and the pump jack was straining with a heavy, uneven load. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0123-0064 showed the wellhead at 18.5 °C with the air at 14.0 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The downhole pump was stuck, most likely from sand or scale. Sandstone Rod & Pump's workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 9 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

Sand and scale build-up in the pump barrel.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 4 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rods and the insert pump.
  3. Inspected the pump: sand in the barrel and a worn plunger.
  4. Ran in a new insert pump.
  5. Re-spaced the pump and hung the rods back on.

Summary of the fix: pulled and replaced downhole pump.

Testing and return to service

Pump test confirmed fluid to surface and the wellhead warmed back to normal. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0123-014

Asset: WELL-0123 (NE-07 Well 123, T200, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: flowline Work started: 25 Sep 2026 08:00 · Finished: 25 Sep 2026 21:00 · Well stopped for this job: 13 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Megan Ward · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0123-0093 on 2026-09-24 Report written: 26 Sep 2026

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0123-0093 at 13:30 on 2026-09-24 found crude oil on the pad: about 10.1% of the pad area, estimated 6.0 bbl. The inspector noted: "Staining along flowline route." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 2.8 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a corrosion hole along the flowline route.

Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak point.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in new line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 228 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 182 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 3.5 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0123-014 (WS-06).
  • 4 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.68% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

The thermal reading at inspection INS-0123-0095 showed the wellhead at 27.8 °C with the air at 22.0 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair.
